---
title: "Optimizing: The SUT Plugin Protocol"
---

MLPerf EDU enforces a strict separation between the referee and the thing
being measured. The harness (LoadGen, telemetry, reporting) is fixed; your
optimization lives in an isolated **System Under Test (SUT)** plugin. Students
never modify the framework to make a workload faster, which is exactly what
makes their speedups comparable.

## The Interface

A plugin is a single Python file containing one class that inherits
`mlperf.sut.SUT_Interface` and implements two methods:

```python
from mlperf.sut import SUT_Interface

class MyOptimizedSUT(SUT_Interface):
    def __init__(self, config):
        # load the model, move it to the device, prepare caches
        ...

    async def process_queries(self, samples):
        # execute a batch of LoadGen QuerySamples; return telemetry
        ...
```

The LoadGen referee drives `process_queries` according to the scenario
(single-stream, server, offline) and measures latency and throughput from the
outside. Whatever you do inside the class, including KV caching, batching,
mixed precision, quantization, or a fused kernel, is your optimization; the
measurement never moves.

## Worked Lab Examples

The repository ships three lab exercises built on this protocol, under
[`examples/`](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/tree/main/mlperf-edu/examples):

| **Lab** | **File** | **What you optimize** |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Lab 1 | `lab1_optimization.py` | Training-loop systems optimization |
| Lab 2 | `lab2_inference_sut.py` | Inference latency (KV cache, batching, precision) |
| Lab 3 | `lab3_arch_comparison.py` | Dense vs. sparse architecture comparison |

Each lab file is itself the plugin. Read the reference implementation, run the
baseline, apply the TODO optimization, and re-run to measure your gain.

::: {.callout-note}
**Status.** The `SUT_Interface` protocol and the lab plugins ship today and are
importable from `mlperf.sut`. First-class `mlperf run --sut <plugin.py>`
wiring in the product CLI is part of the certification release; the labs
currently drive plugins through their own harness entry points as documented
in each lab file.
:::

## Rules for Comparable Submissions

The public-result contract distinguishes closed submissions, which keep the
reference model and dataset fixed and optimize only execution, from open ones,
which may change the model. See [`PUBLIC_RULES.md`](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/blob/main/mlperf-edu/PUBLIC_RULES.md)
for the score-bearing and performance-bearing rules, and run `mlperf audit`
to check a workload's contract before you optimize against it.
